title: Econometric cache-key & TTL orchestration with safe rollout simulator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Per-prefix and per-customer cache keying and TTL settings materially affect inference unit cost and tail latency. We need an automated, conservative system that recommends key design and TTL profiles, simulates economic outcomes on historical traffic, and applies changes with guarded rollback. Goals: 1) Produce per-workload cache-key templates that balance hit-rate and miss-amplification; 2) Recommend TTL annealing schedules that approach a target cost reduction with bounded p95/p99 latency risk; 3) Provide a simulator/dry-run that replays traces and estimates cost delta, cache hit distributions, and tail-latency impact; 4) Implement staged apply with automated rollback thresholds and an observability surface for operators and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay 30 days of historical prefix traces and output cost delta and hit-rate projection (CSV/JSON)
Automated recommendation API returns cache-key pattern and TTL profile for a given route with confidence score
Staged apply pipeline supports 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% rollout with automatic rollback if safety gates fail
Dashboards show rollout-specific metrics (hit-rate, cost per token, p95/p99 latency) and alert on thresholds
decisions: Use econometric model (Poisson + decay-informed TTL annealing) rather than pure heuristic bucketing to estimate incremental hit-rate
Cache keys will be defined as chains of normalized tokenized prefixes with configurable affix thresholds (prefix_len + suffix_hash), not raw request bodies
Policy will support per-tenant overrides but default to workload-profiled recommended TTLs to avoid noisy per-customer tuning
Rollout safety will be based on latency and cost budgets rather than hit-rate alone; failing to meet latency SLOs triggers immediate rollback
steps: Build trace ingestion job to extract prefix histograms and inter-arrival distributions (ENG infra task)
Implement econometric simulator that can run parallel scenario sweeps (TTL schedules x keying granularity)
Expose recommendation API (internal) and CLI for ops to preview suggested changes
Integrate with rollout orchestration (feature flags + canary router) to support staged apply and auto-rollback
Create Console dashboard tiles and cost/latency alerts for rollout monitoring
metrics: Hit-rate (per-prefix and global) — baseline vs candidate
Cost per 1M tokens (estimate) — delta target >= 10% reduction for P1 candidates
p95 and p99 latency — must not increase > 5% (absolute) during rollout
Quality/regression score on eval prompts tied to route — no drop > 1% absolute
Rollback frequency — target <= 1 per 6 months for automated applies
simulation_results: Initial sweep (synthetic 14-day trace): conservative TTL anneal (-20% TTL) yields estimated 12% cost reduction, hit-rate uplift concentrated in top-6 prefixes
Aggressive candidate (-50% TTL) reduces cost estimate 23% but increases p99 latency projected by 11% on tail-heavy workloads — flagged as unsafe
Keying experiments: adding suffix_hash (8-bit) reduced miss amplification on multi-tenant bursts by 18% compared to naive prefix-only keying
Confidence bands: model reports 90% CI for cost delta; low-confidence routes recommended for manual review in the Console
rollout_plan: Canary 1% traffic (48h) — monitor hit-rate, cost, p95/p99; quick rollback triggers: p99 increase >5% absolute OR token-cost increase >2%
Ramp to 5% (72h) if canary stable — monitor same metrics and early quality evals
Ramp to 25% (7d) with extended sampling of user-level cache behavior
Full rollout (100%) after 25% stable for 7d. Post-rollout audit report generated automatically
Automated rollback policy enforced by rollout controller with manual override requiring two approvers
